newsitem.title: FRANCE: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV SETS SECOND WORLD RECORD IN TWO DAYS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV SETS SECOND WORLD RECORD IN TWO DAYS.

text.p: Denis Pankratov, denied two world records in Paris last year because of a dope test blunder, set his second world mark in two days at this year's edition of the same short-course World Cup meeting on Sunday.

The Russian double Olympic champion clocked 51.78 seconds in the 100 metres butterfly, bettering the short-course world record of 51.93 he set last Wednesday in the penultimate meeting of the World Cup series in Imperia, Italy.
Pankratov broke the 50 metres butterfly world short-course mark on Saturday, his time of 23.35 seconds bettering the 23.45 set by Briton Mark Foster in December 1995 in Sheffield, England.
"I like this swimming pool," he said. "It's one of the fastest in Europe. It's certainly one of my favourites and I'm trying to make the most of it."

Pankratov has broken four world short-course records in nine days. He set a 200 butterfly world mark of 1:52.64 at a World Cup meeting in Gelsenkirchen, Germany, on February 1 before breaking the 100 butterfly in Imperia and completing his Paris double.

At last year's World Cup final in Paris he broke both the 100 and 200 butterfly short-course marks only to be denied the records because French meet organisers had run out of bottles to administer the dope tests necessary for ratification.
"I was hurt by what happened last year," Pankratov said on Saturday, referring to the dope test fiasco. "You can't forget that kind of thing."
